description: Family-owned freight forwarder with 140 trucks. Tours are still planned in Excel and delivery notes are on paper. Opened a second depot near Hanover in 2026 and is hiring dispatchers.
Sheet metal and welding supplier for machine builders. Production planning runs on an ERP system introduced in 2004. Management announced plans to double laser-cutting capacity by 2027.
Producer of chilled ready meals for supermarket chains. Quality documentation is kept in paper binders. Retail customers now require digital traceability for every batch.
Injection moulding of plastic parts for the automotive and household sectors. Orders arrive by email and fax and are typed in manually. A new managing director took over in early 2026.
Wholesaler for building materials with eight branches. Stock levels are reconciled once a month by hand. Struggles with rising stock-outs and has started looking for a new inventory system.

Contract logistics provider running three warehouses for retail clients. Warehouse processes rely on paper pick lists. Lost a major client in 2025 due to delivery errors and is reviewing its processes.
Turned and milled precision parts for automotive tier-1 suppliers. Machine data is not recorded centrally. Customers are demanding shorter lead times and real-time order status.
Manufacturer of corrugated cardboard packaging. Production scheduling is done on a whiteboard. Plans to open a new production hall in 2027 and faces a shortage of skilled workers.
Refrigerated transport for pharmaceutical and food customers. Temperature logs are collected on paper and scanned later. New EU documentation rules force the company to digitise its records.
Iron foundry for pumps and valves. Uses separate, unconnected systems for sales, production and accounting. Energy costs rose sharply and management wants transparency on cost drivers.
Producer of delicatessen salads and sauces. Recipes and production orders are managed in spreadsheets. Recently acquired a smaller competitor and needs to merge both sites' processes.
Electronics contract manufacturer for industrial customers. Quality data is collected but not analysed. Wants to reduce scrap rates and has budgeted for an improvement programme in 2027.
Regional freight forwarder specialising in partial loads. No customer portal; shipment status is given by phone. Customers increasingly ask for online tracking.
Supplier of interior components to German car makers. Shift planning is done in Excel for 950 employees. Transition to electric vehicles is changing its product mix and volumes.
Agricultural wholesaler supplying feed and seeds to farmers. Orders are taken by phone and written on paper slips. The owner's daughter took over in 2026 and wants to modernise the business.
Steel trading and cutting service centre. Pricing is calculated manually per order. Volatile steel prices make quick and accurate quotes increasingly important.

Industrial bakery supplying discount retailers across eastern Germany. Production planning relies on the experience of two long-serving planners who retire soon. Management is concerned about losing this knowledge.
Warehouse and fulfilment services for e-commerce brands. Uses a self-built warehouse system that only one IT employee understands. Growing order volumes cause frequent system slowdowns.
Builder of special-purpose machines. Runs SAP ECC, with migration to S/4HANA still open. Mostly stable business with no announced changes.
Small freight forwarder with 30 trucks. Uses a standard transport management software. Owner is open to improvements but has a limited budget.
Precision mechanics for optics and medical technology. Partly digitised: CAD and ERP are connected, shop floor still paper-based. No current growth plans announced.
Regional mineral water and soft drink producer. Introduced a modern filling line in 2024. Sales and logistics processes are still largely manual.
Producer of wooden components for furniture makers. Has a modern ERP but low usage among staff. Management is unsure where to start with further digitalisation.
Wholesaler for sanitary and heating products. Launched an online shop for installers in 2023. Warehouse and route planning are still manual.
Aluminium die casting for powertrain parts. Highly dependent on combustion-engine customers. Currently focusing on cost cutting rather than new projects.
Port logistics and container handling services. Uses a mix of older and newer systems. Recently won a tender that will increase volumes by 20 percent.
Contract manufacturer of specialty chemicals. Strong compliance processes with validated systems. Interested in data analytics for production but has no concrete plans.
Fruit and vegetable wholesaler supplying restaurants. Orders come in via WhatsApp and phone. Small team, owner sceptical about external consultants.
Manufacturer of gearboxes for industrial drives. Has a digitalisation team of two people. Projects so far focused on the sales side.
Cold storage provider for food producers. Uses a modern warehouse system but billing is done by hand. Planning to expand storage capacity in 2028.
Producer of special screws and fasteners. Production is largely automated, administration is not. No information about upcoming changes.
Dairy cooperative processing milk from 600 farms. Supplier payments are calculated in a legacy system. Cooperative decisions are slow, but the board discusses modernisation.
Digital freight platform with its own software team of 60 developers. Fully cloud-based operations and real-time tracking. Builds its technology in-house.
Small family bakery with two shops. Plans to keep the business as it is.
Automation specialist listed on the stock exchange. Runs a fully integrated SAP S/4HANA landscape and has its own data science department.
One-person managed transport business with five vans.
Producer of metal household goods. Filed for insolvency in 2025; operations continue under an administrator.
Large international logistics group with its own consulting arm and a central digital transformation unit.
Vegetable grower selling to regional markets. Seasonal business with minimal administration.
Distributor of business software licences. Highly digitised processes and automated order handling.
Supplier of stamped parts. Management has frozen all external projects for 2026 due to cost-cutting.
Sawmill producing construction timber for local carpenters.
Fully automated fulfilment centre with robotic picking and real-time dashboards for clients.
Meat processor. Recently completed a two-year ERP and MES implementation with an external partner.
Group of six manufacturing companies. Each subsidiary uses its own outdated systems and paper-based quality checks. The holding wants to harmonise processes across all sites.
Describes itself as 'digital pioneer' on its website after introducing email order confirmations in 2021. Tours are still planned on paper maps.

Contract manufacturer of surgical instruments. Strict medical device regulation requires extensive documentation, currently handled with paper forms. Regulatory audits found documentation gaps in 2025.
Freight forwarder whose website mentions 'AI-based route optimisation'. The feature is a pilot used for one customer only; dispatchers plan all other tours manually.
Steelmaker with outdated production systems and strong pressure to cut energy costs. Currently in negotiations about a sale to an international group.
Office supplies wholesaler. Digital ordering for customers is advanced, but the warehouse runs on handwritten pick lists and errors are rising.
